cases.title: Someone outside the household pays a utility bill as a loan she must repay in full
cases.part: B.4, Example: Lender outside the household; G.4.c
cases.ssa_answer: The loan amount is $150 and she repays all of it, so the repayment equals the value of the help and she receives no outside in-kind support.

cases.title: A utility bill paid as a loan, repaid only for her share of a household of two
cases.part: B.4, Example: Lender outside the household; G.4.a and G.4.c
cases.ssa_answer: As if there were no loan, her share of the $150 bill in a household of two is $75. She repays $75, which equals that value, so she receives no outside in-kind support.

cases.title: Someone outside pays the electric bill for a household of three
cases.ssa_answer: $100 is countable as in-kind support: the $300 bill divided among the three members of the household, which is under the presumed maximum value.

cases.title: Food and shelter from an adult child, to be repaid only if SSI is paid
cases.part: B.3, Example 2: Conditional requirement for repayment
cases.ssa_answer: There is no bona fide loan, because repayment depends on SSI being paid. The food and shelter are in-kind support under the normal rules; with both from the household and nothing paid toward it, the one-third reduction applies.

cases.title: Food and shelter from a parent she feels bound to repay, though the parent expects nothing
cases.part: B.3, Example 1: No obligation for repayment
cases.ssa_answer: There is no bona fide loan, because the two never agreed that Jane must repay. The food and shelter are in-kind support under the normal rules; with both from the household and nothing paid toward it, the one-third reduction applies.

cases.title: Food and shelter from a sibling under a repayment plan she cannot meet
cases.part: B.5, Example 2: Prorata share greater than anticipated income
cases.ssa_answer: The repayment plan is not feasible, so the loan is not a bona fide loan of in-kind support, and the food and shelter count under the normal rules; with both from the household and nothing paid toward it, the one-third reduction applies.

cases.title: After a loan of food and shelter ends, he pays his full share
cases.ssa_answer: His contribution equals or exceeds his pro rata share, so he is in federal living arrangement A with no in-kind support, and the full SSI amount is paid.

cases.title: After a loan of food and shelter ends, he pays $300 of a $400 share
cases.part: E.4, Example: Simultaneous development claim with RT diary for re-contact
cases.ssa_answer: He pays less than his pro rata share, so he is in federal living arrangement B and subject to the one-third reduction.

cases.title: A sibling sends cash toward the household's costs, and he pays his full share
cases.part: G, Example 1: Claimant's Contribution Equals Their Pro Rata Share
cases.ssa_answer: Mabel's $100 to John is cash income, not in-kind support, even though it pays household costs. John's contribution equals his pro rata share, so he receives no in-kind support.

cases.title: A sibling sends cash toward the household's costs, and he pays less than his share
cases.part: G, Example 2: Claimant's Contribution Does Not Equal Their Pro Rata Share
cases.ssa_answer: Mabel's $100 is cash income, and because John pays only $200 of his $300 share he is also subject to the one-third reduction: at 2026 rates, $994 less $331.33, less the $100 after the $20 general exclusion, $582.67.

cases.title: Paying $100 toward a $150 share of an apartment's costs
cases.part: G, Example 1: Pro rata share exceeds the contribution by $20 or more
cases.ssa_answer: His share exceeds what he pays by at least $20, so he receives in-kind support valued at the one-third reduction (federal living arrangement B).

cases.title: Paying $175 toward a $150 share of an apartment's costs
cases.part: G, Example 2: Contribution exceeds the pro rata share by $20
cases.ssa_answer: He pays more than his share, so he is in a sharing arrangement (federal living arrangement A) with no in-kind support from the household.

cases.title: Paying $125 toward a verified $145 share of an apartment's costs
cases.part: G, Example 3: Contribution is within $20 of the pro rata share
cases.ssa_answer: What he pays is within $20 of his share, so a sharing arrangement exists: federal living arrangement A with no in-kind support.

cases.title: Paying $150 a month, half for food and half for shelter, in a nephew's apartment
cases.part: C.4, Example: Determining if double earmarking applies
cases.ssa_answer: Neither earmarked payment meets its share, so she receives food and shelter throughout the month from the household and is subject to the one-third reduction.

cases.title: A charity gives a child with a life-threatening condition a timeshare
cases.ssa_answer: The timeshare is an in-kind gift from a tax-exempt organization to a child with a life-threatening condition, so its $15,000 value is not counted as income in the month it is received.
